questions.stem: Why does bile neutralise stomach acid in the small intestine?

options.text: To dissolve the food so it can be absorbed
To provide the alkaline conditions needed for enzymes in the small intestine to work
To kill bacteria that survived the stomach
To activate pepsin in the small intestine

questions.explanation: Bile is alkaline and neutralises the acid from the stomach. This creates the slightly alkaline conditions (around pH 8) needed for enzymes like pancreatic lipase and amylase to work at their optimum.
